newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St Barbara Mines chairman resigns.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St Barbara Mines chairman resigns.

text.p: St Barbara Mines Ltd chairman Alan Birchmore said on Tuesday he would resign as both chairman and a director of the Perth-based gold miner.
Birchmore, who last week announced his intention to sell up to a 19.9 percent stake in the company, said in a statement he believed his immediate resignation was in St Barbara's best interests.
A Western Australian court last week issued orders for the settlement of a long-running dispute over shareholdings in Bengal Star Pty Ltd, which holds 53 percent of St Barbara.
Bengal Star is jointly owned by Birchmore and former St Barbara operations manager Ross Atkins. The court order enabled Birchmore and Atkins to each dispose of up to 19.9 percent of St Barbara.
The two men have been in dispute since Atkins was dismissed as operations director more than a year ago.
Birchmore said on Tuesday the decision to leave the company was difficult, given an increase in resources at the mine.
"It is an exciting time for St Barbara and in normal circumstances, not a moment I would choose to leave," he said.
"However, we have not enjoyed normal circumstances for more than a year now and the company must be given the opportunity to put discord and strife behind."
